newsitem.title: UK: UK gas output falls in August, but up year on year.
newsitem.headline: UK gas output falls in August, but up year on year.

text.p: U.K. gas production in August fell to 4,669 million cubic feet per day (MMcfd), its lowest level this year and down from 4,917 MMcfd in July, analysts Wood Mackenzie said. But although August production fell from July, it was still almost 25 percent higher than the August 1995 level of 3,740 MMcfd.
This increase is reflected in the long term trend: average output in the year from September 1995 to August 1996 was 7,989 MMcfd, up from 6,619 MMcfd in the same period of the previous year.
Wood Mackenzie said increased use of gas to fuel power generation was behind the continued surge in production.
The fall in output in August from July was explained by the seasonally low demand in the summer as well as by maintenance continuing from July into August.

The Alwyn North area production fell to 165 MMcfd in August, from 393 MMcfd in July because of a three-week scheduled operational programme. Production at Bruce fell to 231 MMcfd from 562 MMcfd in July. Piper and Nelson output also fell.
Maintenance reduced output at Markham, which produced no gas at all in August, and at Clipper, where production fell by 107 MMcfd to 76 MMcfd.
The giant Morecambe field produced no gas for the third month running in August.
Wood Mackenzie said July was the first month of a new six-monthly Petroleum Revenue Tax period, so it was unlikely that the field's tax position was driving its output level.
